text:
nina: ran a CI-scale continuous-batching run on the kv-heavy workload this morning. saw an out-of-memory at ~62s into the 512-step sequence window. suspicion: batch growth + workspace reservation not reclaimed quickly. attaching short profiler excerpt below.

sarah: ugh. is this on the new allocator tune (shrink-to-fit enabled)?

nina: yes, shrink-to-fit was on. allocator logs show repeated large reservations that never fully compact between minibatches. sample: 
```
[alloc] reserve 24.3GB -> commit 22.1GB
[free] deferred_free_queue len=128, reclaimed 80MB
[alloc] reserve 24.3GB -> commit 23.5GB
[oom_guard] peak 23.9GB
```

miguel: that deferred_free_queue stalling is interesting. could be because KV cache refs keep buffers pinned until end-of-seq. Do we have per-seq refcounts?

nina: we dump per-seq meta: "kv_refcount" shows ~1 for most, but long-tails at 5-7 for a subset of sequences (likely reranked candidates). each extra ref keeps a 1.6MB buffer alive. multiplies across batches.

raj: also check pad churn: continuous batching grows batch size over time as new requests join; padding to max-len in the batch causes wasted workspace. how much pad waste?

nina: measured padding waste ~= 2.1GB at the crash point. breakdown:
- active payloads: 12.4GB
- padding overhead: 2.1GB
- allocator fragmentation: ~0.9GB
- bookkeeping & per-seq metadata: ~0.3GB

miguel: so combined (pad + frag + refs) ~3.3GB headroom lost. That's the delta between reserve and commit. If shrink-to-fit only triggers on full GC, continuous inflow prevents it.

sarah: idea: proactive workspace trim when batch growth stops for N cycles. or evict low-priority KV entries aggressively once pad fraction > X.

nina: attempted a quick patch: after each minibatch, if pad_fraction > 0.25 and growth_rate < 0.02, call workspace.shrink(target=committed*0.85). result: run extended by ~45s before OOM (not ideal).

miguel: nice. can we free per-seq metadata earlier? maybe move metadata to a compact arena and free on token commit instead of end-of-seq? reduces per-seq overhead.

raj: there's also kernel selection side: some kernels allocate temp workspace per invocation. if continuous batching favors a kernel with larger transient workspace under certain seq_len distribution, it could amplify this. Any profiler kernel breakdown?

nina: yes. nsight sampling shows that the matmul kernel selected for long sequences kept a fallback path that allocates a temporary 512MB buffer for permute ops. when switched to alternative kernel variant (permute-in-place) transient allocs disappeared and peak dropped ~700MB.

sarah: so immediate levers: 1) avoid kernel variants with large transient allocs for continuous batches; 2) add a soft-trim policy for workspace; 3) change KV ref lifecycle to release earlier for low-importance keys.

miguel: operationally, we should also add a perf regression test that simulates slow-growing continuous batches + rare long-tail refs. capture peak reserved vs commit over time.

nina: agreed. I'll push two PRs: allocator soft-trim + kernel variant preference toggle. also a short patch to log per-seq refcounts to ventilate hidden pinning.

raj: assign owners?

nina: PR1 (allocator soft-trim) -> @miguel. PR2 (kernel variant pref) -> @sarah. per-seq ref logging -> me.

deploy-bot: deploy preview created for branch nina/cont-batch-trim. link: https://ci.internal/previews/2461 :white_check_mark:

sarah: thanks. let's run the CI workload and reconvene if the tail behavior changes. if we still hit OOM, next step is to prototype an aggressive KV compact-on-idle which merges small key blobs into pooled buffers.

miguel: marking follow-ups: add perf test, observe pad_fraction threshold tuning, experiment with per-seq metadata arena.

nina: noted. will post perf graphs after the preview run completes (should be in ~1hr). :hourglass_flowing_sand:
